counterfactual_missing_items: No delta waves or atrioventricular accessory-pathway physiology are described, so an accessory pathway is not supported.
No irregular fibrillatory activation is present; the rhythm has a stable atrial cycle length of 280 ms with P waves.
The reentrant circuit is not separate from the mitral annulus and prior mitral isthmus ablation line; entrainment and activation map place it around that structure.
decisive_items: counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus and left atrial appendage
postpacing intervals within 20 ms of the tachycardia cycle length at the inferior and lateral mitral annulus and at the left atrial appendage–left pulmonary vein ridge
recordings showed activation within the vein of Marshall that matched the tachycardia cycle length
response.rationale: C1 combines the mitr-isthmus-dependent flutter mechanism with the explicitly mapped CCW direction; entrainment evidence places the circuit around the mitral annulus/ridge and the vein-of-Marshall activation supplies the epicardial continuation across the scar. R1 is the same diagnosis without the supported directional modifier. R5 is overbroad, R2 mistakenly elevates the VOM epicardial route to an accessory pathway without pre-excitation, and R4 uses only the historical diagnosis of AF rather than current regular perimitral flutter behavior.

rejected.why: Generic scar-related AT omits the specific perimitral flutter circuit shown by the activation map and entrainment.
Current findings are a regular 280 ms atrial tachycardia with P waves and macro-reentrant activation, not AF.
The epicardial route is a Marshall-related continuation of the atrial flutter circuit, not an atrioventricular accessory pathway with pre-excitation.
